chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us via this chain from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There are two cries; one at the beginning of the night, and one at the end of the second night.' I asked: 'How will that be?' He said: 'One will be from the Heaven, and one from Iblis.' I said: 'And how will one be distinguished from the other?' He said: 'He who has heard of them before they occur will know which is which.'

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ الثَّانِيَةِ: The end of the second night

ai.seo_question: What are the two cries mentioned before the appearance of the Mahdi and how to distinguish them?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the two cries preceding the appearance of Imam al-Mahdi (aj) are distinguished by their origin: one is a divine signal from the heavens, while the other is a deceptive cry from Iblis. The Imam notes that those who have previously heard these specific sounds can differentiate them, highlighting the importance of prior knowledge and spiritual awareness in recognizing the signs of the Occultation's end. This distinction underscores the dual nature of the pre-appearance era, where truth and deception may sound similar to the unprepared.
